chapter_title: Concerning Wisdom; it is far superior when on the
spiritual_reading:
# Spiritual Translation of the Kephalaia Chapter on Wisdom Proclaimed

---

**¶1:** Behold, when a person receives divine truth into the will and fixes it within his understanding as a principle of faith, you will find the will delighting greatly in what it has received. However, [sh]all his [GAP-1: interior delight increase] to him, more th[an] when he may bri[GAP-2: ng it forth into expression] and communicate it outwardly. He shall be illuminated by it, and [t]hat [GAP-3: divine truth] shall radiate the more fully within him. It is uncovered before his understanding, and through it he takes on spiritual capacity and the power of truth conjoined with good.

---

**¶2:** I perceive [GAP-4: clearly] that this truth I have communicated outwardly is genuine. I know that the divine truth I have received inwardly has pervaded my will and been completed throughout my whole mind. Yet it does not appear as full spiritual radiance within me — so that I recognize it as having advanced — except when I bring it forth through outward expression and communicate it to others. Indeed, when I communicate it, I deliver it to the receptive faculties [GAP-5: of] others that they may receive it in obedience. Would I do these same things, even if I had never received these truths during [GAP-6: my] earlier states of spiritual life? Would I desire intensely, and would my will be drawn toward the divine truth I now communicate? [I entreat y]ou, my teacher, that you would instruct me as to [GAP-7: why] this divine truth becomes more fully developed when I bring it into outward expression than when it remains sealed within the will alone.

---

**¶3:** [GAP-8: For indeed] it is more fully present in outward expression when I communicate it than when it remains concealed within the wi[ll]. You yourself experience delight in it; and the other who receives it from you — he too shall experience delight in it, and be illuminated [GAP-9: by] it, and thereby gain enduring spiritual strength.

---

**¶4:** For this matter is like this: just as a new truth that is conceived within the interior will. It [GAP-10: stirs and] turns within the interior affection, filling the whole capacity of the will. The affection that bears it perceives and understands that this living truth she carries is alive within her. She delights over it until [the tim]e when she brings it forth into manifest life. And it comes forth from her alive, with all its [GAP-11: faculties whole] and perfect in form, without deficiency, [GAP-12: into] the open sphere of spiritual freedom, which is far more expansive than the confined interior state in which it first existed. It fills the understanding with the light of truth and speaks with the living voice of spiritual expression in the manner of all truths that are brought to birth.

---

**¶5:** Now, the time when the affection conceives this new truth within the interior will — her delight at carrying it inwardly is not so [ve]ry great as when she brings it forth and beholds it manifest; and is filled with its [be]auty and fullness in a single moment of perception. The love and delight over it shall be a hundredfold greater than before, now that she has brought it forth into the light and beheld it openly.

---

**¶6:** For the first time, when the affection conceived it within the interior will, its spiritual beauty and the sight of its illuminating quality were hidden from the bearing affection. But when she brought it forth, she beheld its beauty. Its fullness and loveliness came before the understanding of its intellectual origin and its nurturing affection and all their kindred states of good and truth. They shall delight over it more and more when they perceive it directly, face to face, and behold its beauty and the delight it gives.

---

**¶7:** Just as in this likeness, the divine truth that is present [GAP-13: in] the will of a person is like the living new truth that is co[nceived] within the interior affection. And when he is taught and seals it within his will, it becomes like the new truth that is brought forth into manifest life, and they behold its spiritual beauty.

---

**¶8:** So, in this way, the divine truth that the person communicates, speaking it forth from his will, shall advance more and mor[e]. Its increase and glory shall be multiplied from the time when the beauty and radiance of the expressed truth is displayed before the understanding [of th]ose who receive it, and it shall also advance for you [GAP-14: through] your own reception, and you are astonished at what you communicate.

---

**¶9:** Once again, divine truth is like this while it remains hidden within the will of a person. [Bef]ore he has expressed it outwardly, it is just like [GAP-15: the latent love] that is concealed within natural perception. An[d] that natural perception is [GAP-16: enkindled] by the latent love within it, but the external form of lov[e that dwells in] the natural perception is not apparent. Indeed, you can see [GAP-17: many such natural] perceptions, and they are gathered together in a single mind. It is impossible to [illu]minate that mind as long as the light within [GAP-18: them remains latent,] until the time when they are brought to the love, and the illumination [comes f]orth from them. It is possible for that entire mind [GAP-19: to be] illuminated by the light proceeding from a single perception enkindled by love.

---

**¶10:** This is also the case with the divine truth that is within the will of a person. [GAP-20: It] is like the love that is concealed within natural perception, whose illuminating power is not [d]isplayed. For its part, the divine truth is like this: its illumination is hidden and its glory is concealed in the will; but when the person will communicate it outwardly, its glory shall be displayed before the understanding and the receptive faculties of a multitude.

---

**¶11:** So, if divine truth is like the paradigms you have taught me, why are there some people who shall receive the communication of divine truth and delight in it and give glory to it, when others shall hear it and neither delight [i]n it nor receive any glory from it amongst themselves?

---

**¶13:** For in this respect divine truth is like this new truth about which I have told you, the one that [GAP-21: was] brought forth from the bearing affection. Now, when it is brought forth, its intellectual origin and its nurturing affection and all their kindred states shall delight over it. However, you find others who grieve on account of it, [s]ince they are alien to it. These are not counted among its kindred states of good and truth. [They do n]ot delight over it, because it is not of their spiritual lineage.

---

**¶14:** This is also [GAP-22: the case] with divine truth. When it is communicated through the outward expression of the one who teaches, those who are [a]kin to it in their interior states shall receive it unto themselves and delight in it; but [GAP-23: those] who are alien to it neither delight in it [GAP-24: nor understand it,] nor receive it unto themselves.

---

**¶15:** Just like the illumination of [GAP-25: the love, which I] described to you, that shall come forth from the natural perception [and become apparent o]utwardly before the understanding of every one. So, [wh]oever looks with understanding shall see the illumination that has [come fro]m the perception; but whoever is without understanding does not perceive the [lov]e.

---

**¶16:** This is also the case with divine truth when it is communicated. The person in whom dwells the interior rational faculty — to him belongs the divine truth. Whenever he may hear it, he shall receive it into himself; but the one who has no interior rational faculty within him is a stranger to it. He neither receives it into himself, nor shall he attend to [GAP-26: it].

---

*Summary of the spiritual sense:* This chapter teaches that divine truth received into the will exists at first as a living but hidden potency — like an unborn perception, like love latent in natural knowledge. It achieves its full spiritual life only when it is brought forth into outward expression and communicated, whereupon it multiplies in radiance for both the one who communicates and those who receive. Yet only those whose interior states are kindred to it — those possessing the interior rational faculty — can receive and delight in it. Those in alien states, lacking the rational faculty, remain as the spiritually blind before a light they cannot perceive.

reconstructions.reconstructed_text: Behold, when a person will be taught wise wisdom in his heart, and he seals it in his doctrine, so shall you find him rejoicing greatly about it. However, [sh]all his [joy be advanced] to him, more th[an] when he may pro-c[laim it] and utter it. He shall be enlightened by it, and [t]hat [wisdom] shall shine forth the more in him. It is un-veil[ed be]fore him, and through it he assumes power and truth.

I understand [well] that this word I have uttered is correct. I know that the wis-dom I have been taught is spread through my heart and perfected in my soul. (However), it is not found like the splendour in me, so that I regard it [ad]vanced, except when I shall proclaim it by my mouth and utter it to others. Indeed, when I proclaim it, I am giving it to the ears [of] others to hear. Would I do these same things, even if I had never heard it in [my] days of being? Would I desire greatly and my heart be drawn to the wis-dom I now proclaim? [I entreat y]ou, my master, that you might instruct me as to [why] this wisdom becomes more advanced when I proclaim it, than when it is sealed in my heart.

[For indeed] it is superior in my mouth when I proclaim it than when it is set in m[y heart]. You yourself rejoice in it; and the other one who hears it from you, he shall rejoice in it, and be enlightened [by] it and receive thereby permanent strength.

For like this matter, just so a small b[o]y who is conceived in the belly of his mother. He [stirs and he] turns in his mother's womb, filling her womb. The mother knows and understands that this child she conceives is alive within her. She rejoices over him until [the tim]e when she gives birth. And he comes from her alive with his [limbs whole] and perfect in beauty, without defect, [in] the living open air that is more sp[ac]ious than the first air he was in. He fills his eyes with the light and speaks with his living voice in the way of they who are born.

Now, the time when this woman conceives the child in her belly, her joy at conceiving him in her womb is not so [ve]ry great as when she gives birth and sees him; and is full of his [be]auty and stature in the space of a single moment. The love and joy over him shall be a hundred [t]imes greater than it was, now that she has given birth and seen him.

For the first time when she conceived him in her belly, his beauty and the sight of his eyes was hidden from his m[o/th]er; but when she gave birth to him she saw his beauty. His s[t]ature and his loveliness came before the e[ye]s of his f[athe]r [a]nd his mother and all his relatives. They shall rejoic[e] over him more and more when they look upon him face to face and see his beauty and delightfulness.

Just as in this simile, the wisdom that is present [in] the heart of the person is like the living child who is co[nceived] in the belly of his mother. And when he is taught and seals it in his heart, it becomes like the child who shall be born, and they see his beauty.

So, in this way, the wisdom that the person proclaims, speak[ng] it from his heart, shall be advanced more and mor[e]. Its en-hancement and glory shall double from the time when the bea-uty and splendour of the saying will be displayed before the eyes [of t]hey who hear it, and it shall also advance for you [who proclaim it, through] your hearing, and you are astonished at what you proclai[m].

Once again, the wisdom is like this, while it is hidden in the heart of the person. [Bef]ore he has uttered it, it is just like [the blaze] of fire that is hidden in wood. An[d] that wood is [set aflame] by the blaze of the fire, but the garment of fir[e that exists in] the wood is not apparent. Indeed, you can see [much] wood and they put them in a single house. It is impossible to [put li]ght to that house as long as the light within [them is hidden] until the time when they are added to the fire, and the light [comes f]orth from them. It is possible for that entire house [to be] lit by the light of a single piece of wood.

This is also the case with the wisdom that is in the heart of the person. [It] is like the fire that is hidden in the wood, as its light is not [d]isplayed. For its part, the wisdom is like this: its li[ght] is hidden and its glory is hidden in the heart; but when the person will proclaim it, its glory shall be displayed before the eyes and the ears of a multitude.

So, if the wisdom is like the paradigms you have taught me, why are there some people who shall hear the word of wisdom and rejoice in it and give glory to it; when others shall listen to it and neither rejoice [i]n it nor receive glory amongst them?

For in this respect the wisdom is like this child about whom I have told you, the one who [was] born from the woman. Now, when he will be born, his father and mother and family circle shall rejoice over him. However, you find others grieving by reason of him, [s]ince they are strangers to him. These are not reckoned among his family. [They do n]ot rejoice over him, because he is not of their race.

This is also [the case] with the wisdom. When it is proclaimed by the mouth of the teacher, these who are [a]kin to it shall receive it to them and rejoice in it; but [those] who are strangers to it neither rejoice in it [nor give glory to it] nor receive it to them.

Just like the light of [the fire, which I] proclaim[ed] to you, that shall come from the wood [and be apparent o]utside before the eyes of every one. So, [wh]oever looks shall see the light that has [come fro]m the wood; but whoever is blind does not see the [fir]e.

This is also the case with the wisdom, when it will be pro-claimed. The person, in whom is the [Mi]nd, of him is the wisdom. Whenever he may hear it, he shall receive it in to him; but the one who has no Mind in him is a stranger to it. He neither receives it in to him, nor shall he listen to [it].

fills.explanation: The spiritual reading says "interior delight increase"; "joy be advanced" uses the chapter's own vocabulary ("advanced" recurs in ¶2 and ¶8) to express the increase of interior delight when wisdom passes from sealed state to proclamation.
Completing "proclaim it" to match the recurring phrase pattern "proclaim it and utter it" used throughout the chapter.
The spiritual reading identifies "divine truth" which in the Kephalaia's natural register is consistently rendered as "wisdom" throughout this entire chapter.
The spiritual reading says "clearly"; "well" is the standard Kephalaia adverb for clear perception, fitting "I understand well that this word I have uttered is correct."
Confirms the editor's preposition connecting "ears" to "others" in the standard construction "the ears of others to hear."
Confirms the possessive pronoun; the speaker refers to his own past experience in "my days of being."
Confirms the interrogative adverb; the student asks the reason why wisdom advances more when proclaimed than when sealed.
The spiritual reading says "For indeed"; this standard Kephalaia connective introduces the master's confirmatory response to the student's question about proclaimed wisdom.
Confirms the preposition of agency in the standard construction "be enlightened by it."
The spiritual reading says "stirs and turns"; the child stirs and turns in the womb, a standard description of fetal movement corresponding to living truth moving within the interior will.
Confirms the editor's phrase; in the natural register the child is born with whole limbs, corresponding spiritually to complete faculties of the newly born truth.
Confirms the editor's preposition; the child is born "in the living open air," denoting the expansive external sphere into which truth emerges.
Confirms the editor's preposition; wisdom is present "in the heart" of the person, the standard Kephalaia expression for truth dwelling within the will.

The spiritual reading says "through your own reception"; wisdom advances for you who proclaim it through your own hearing — the proclaimer is astonished by their own words, confirming that outward expression enhances the speaker's own reception.
Confirms the editor's phrase; "the blaze of fire hidden in wood" is the natural-register expression for latent love concealed within natural knowledge.

Confirms the editor's phrase; the wood is set aflame (enkindled inwardly) by the latent fire, though its outward garment is not yet apparent — corresponding to natural perception stirred by hidden love.
The spiritual reading says "many such natural perceptions"; in the natural register, "much wood" describes the multiplicity of wood pieces containing latent fire, gathered together in one house.

The spiritual reading says "them remains latent"; the light within the wood pieces is hidden until they are added to fire — using "hidden," the chapter's consistent term for latent spiritual content (¶9, ¶10).
Confirms the editor's infinitive; "It is possible for that entire house to be lit" is the standard passive construction.
Confirms the editor's pronoun; "It is like the fire" begins the standard Kephalaia comparison formula referring back to wisdom.
Confirms the editor's past tense verb; "the one who was born from the woman" refers back to the child simile already narrated.
Confirms the editor's phrase; "This is also the case with the wisdom" is the standard Kephalaia transition formula used repeatedly in this chapter (¶10, ¶14, ¶16).
Confirms the editor's demonstrative pronoun; "but those who are strangers to it" contrasts with "these who are akin to it" in the preceding clause.

The spiritual reading says "nor understand it"; in the natural register, "give glory" parallels ¶11's vocabulary where hearers "give glory to" wisdom, and its negation here mirrors that passage's negative formulation.
Confirms the editor's phrase; the master refers back to the fire-in-wood simile he previously described, using "the fire" as the natural-register term corresponding to love/illumination.
Confirms the editor's pronoun; "nor shall he listen to it" completes the parallel negative construction — the one without Mind neither receives nor attends to wisdom.
